card: This pull request expands the util::Result template to support structured failure types, multiple error and warning messages, and in-place updating to merge results from sequential calls. Previously, util::Result could only return a single bilingual error string without structured failure data, forcing functions like LoadChainstate and wallet loading to rely on ad-hoc tuples and out-parameters to handle distinct failure modes. As an initial application, it migrates chainstate loading and verification to use util::Result, while reducing the class memory footprint by heap-allocating failure objects. Followup PRs #25722 and #29700 depend on these features to standardize error and warning propagation in wallet loading and kernel fatal error handling.
evidence: PR description: 'This is a key missing feature that makes the result class not useful for functions like LoadChainstate() which produce different errors that need to be handled differently.'
PR description and stack facts show this serves as the foundational infrastructure for wallet loading refactoring (#25722) and kernel fatal-error status handling (#29700).
problem: util::Result previously only returned a success value or a single bilingual error string, making it unusable for functions that produce structured error codes requiring distinct caller handling, such as distinguishing recoverable reindex errors from fatal failures in chainstate loading. Functions needing multiple errors, warnings, or structured failure codes relied on ad-hoc return tuples or output parameters.
scope_notes: Adds generic template machinery and message handling in src/util/result.h and src/util/messages.h, accompanied by comprehensive unit tests in src/test/result_tests.cpp, while refactoring chainstate initialization signatures across node, init, and bitcoinkernel.
summary: Expands util::Result to support structured failure types, multiple error and warning messages, and an update method to merge result states while preserving messages. The memory footprint of util::Result is reduced by heap-allocating failure data. The new functionality is applied to chainstate loading and verification functions in place of custom status tuples.
